## boardui
BoardUI is a React + Tailwind CSS v4 design system (Next.js first) with free components and paid Pro components/templates. This server installs component source directly into the user's project — no terminal needed.

Typical flow:
1. In a project without BoardUI, call init_boardui once (installs Tailwind v4 + runtime deps, writes styles/ and utils/).
2. Discover with list_components; read source/props with get_component; get working code with get_usage_examples.
3. Install with install_components — it writes the files and installs npm deps.

Component names are exact — when unsure, call list_components instead of guessing.

## RTL Support

BoardUI supports Arabic, Hebrew, and other right-to-left languages across free components, Pro blocks, and templates. The same source handles RTL and LTR; there is no RTL CLI flag or separate component version.

1. Read get_component and get_usage_examples for the free `direction` item. Install it with install_components (stdio), or write its source and dependencies yourself (read-only HTTP). CLI equivalent: `npx boardui@latest add direction`.
2. Wrap the app with DirectionProvider using an explicit BCP 47 locale: `ar` for Arabic, `he` for Hebrew, `en-US` for English. Set matching `lang` and `dir` on `<html>` for a full-app RTL layout. CSS dir alone does not configure React Aria keyboard navigation, calendars, or portalled menus.

```tsx
import { DirectionProvider } from "@/components/foundations/direction/direction";

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="ar" dir="rtl">
      <body>
        <DirectionProvider locale="ar">{children}</DirectionProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

3. Use logical styles such as ps/pe, ms/me, start/end, and text-start/text-end. Mirror navigation arrows and drawer motion; preserve physical coordinates for charts, canvas, and decorative art. Custom portals should carry `dir={useDirection()}` on their root. Nest DirectionProvider for mixed-language regions.
4. Keep email addresses, URLs, OTP digits, and code LTR; isolate mixed text with bdi or dir=auto. Choose fonts with Arabic or Hebrew coverage and avoid extra letter spacing for Arabic. Translate application labels and accessible names in the application's translation layer; use Intl for dates, numbers, and currencies. Optional `template-copy` supplies TemplateCopyProvider for translating template display copy. Chinese (`zh-CN`) remains LTR.
5. For older installations, refresh the provider, component source, shared dependencies, and global styles. Preserve customizations before using overwrite. Pro updates use the licensed CLI or updated source downloads.

Setup and live Arabic/Hebrew examples: https://www.boardui.com/rtl

Design rules (always apply when writing UI in a BoardUI project): style with BoardUI's semantic Tailwind tokens, never raw palette classes or hex — text via text-text-primary/-secondary/-tertiary, surfaces via bg-background-*-default/-hover, borders via border-border-* and border-separator-border, icons via text-foreground-icon-*. Type uses composite utilities (text-title-2-medium, text-headline-medium, text-body-medium, ...) that set size/weight/line-height together — never rebuild them from text-sm font-medium. Dark mode flips tokens automatically via the .dark class; never hardcode dark: colors. Merge classes with cx() from @/utils/cx (or the utils alias configured in boardui.json); icons from @remixicon/react as component references. init_boardui installs these rules as always-on files (AGENTS.md + .cursor/rules/boardui.mdc) so they survive beyond this session; install_rules adds them to an already initialized project.

Monorepos/custom aliases: put boardui.json next to the destination package's package.json, and pass that package as projectDir. Installs read its paths/aliases and keep npm dependencies in that package. Pass projectDir to get_component and get_usage_examples too for matching source and examples. Package exports and each consuming app's stylesheet/Tailwind setup must already be wired by th… [truncated]

<?claude block s1?>

Character sheets: call get_workflow_instructions with { workflow: "character-sheet" }; websites/apps/games: call get_workflow_instructions with { workflow: "website-builder-flow" }. Character sheets require explicit requests. Bundled files: get_workflow_bundle_file. For AI Influencer chat creation, use ai_influencer_get_options for explicit traits, ai_influencer_list_presets for examples, or ai_influencer_get_settings with job_id for an existing sheet. ai_influencer_prepare returns design and price without generation. Preserve references and seed; use randomize=false for exact settings. Pass prepared params unchanged to ai_influencer_generate with max_credits at the quote or a lower user budget. Existing creation intent permits proceeding within budget; preview-only requests must stop after preparation. For explicit free-only intent, require known available free_gens_remaining and use_free_gens=true with max_credits=0; never fall back to credits. For variants, prepare each sheet and respect total count and aggregate budget. The generator opens an auto-updating widget for progress and the completed sheet. Wait with jobs_wait (timeout_seconds <= 15); do not duplicate the display with show_generation_by_ids or job_display unless explicitly requested. Offer Genjutsu animation afterward unless declined; require agreement and selection of the exact completed character before get_presets source=genjutsu category=genjutsu with initial_inputs.character_sheet=[{id:job_id,type:image_job}]. Opening that gallery does not authorize video submission. If chat creation is unavailable, report it without silently switching to generic image generation or the builder UI. When unsure which model fits, call models_explore(action:'recommend') before calling a generate_* tool. Use virality_predictor when the user asks to predict video virality or analyze engagement, attention, audience response, retention risk, hook strength, or creative performance. For other existing-asset edits use upscale_image/video, outpaint_image, reframe, remove_background, relight_image, or motion_control (single-character Kling recast). For voice creation in Apps UI-capable clients, call create_voice … [truncated]

## slide-studio
First call list_editors and use the registered local browser tab. Never open or connect CarouselBot through a sandboxed agent browser. If no editor is listed, retry briefly because browser reconnection is automatic, then ask the user to open https://carousel.bot in their normal browser and click Connect AI. Companion compatibility and reconnects are automatic. Do not parallel-retry an action that reports an unsupported internal action; retry once after list_editors so automatic recovery can finish. Never restart a healthy companion for a transient editor disconnect. Before edits call get_design_guidance, then begin_edit_session; pass editSessionId to every edit and end it in cleanup. Parallel workers can share the same browser tab and project; sessions track targets without exclusive locks. Use render_slide to inspect actual pixels.

- animate: Build an animation from scratch, making the decisions in the order that determines whether it feels right — should it animate at all, what purpose, which tool, which properties, which curve and duration, how it interrupts, how it exits. Writes the implementation. Use when asked to animate something, add motion, make a component feel alive, or build a transition. For critiquing existing motion use review-animations; for auditing a whole codebase use improve-animations.
- animation-vocabulary: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one.

# Large multi-feature tasks

When a request is big — multiple features, or a large ask that naturally splits into independent
pieces of work — do not implement it as one monolithic pass. Split it into separate commits, one
per feature/unit of work, and drive each unit through this graph-engineering framework using the
Agent tool:

```
Task -> Planner -> Worker -> [Reviewer 1, Reviewer 2, ... Reviewer N] -> Synthesise -> Pass?
                     ^                                                        |
                     |-------------------- feedback (no) ---------------------|
                                                                               |
                                                                          (yes) -> commit -> next unit
```

- **Planner**: breaks the overall ask into an ordered list of commit-sized units of work (a
  Plan Reviewer can review the plan itself before execution starts; route its feedback back to
  the Planner and send a summary of plan feedback to the user).
- **Worker**: a resident agent (kept alive across the reviewer round for a given unit) that
  implements one unit of work.
- **Reviewers (1..N)**: spawn multiple reviewer agents in parallel against the Worker's output —
  e.g. correctness, simplification/efficiency, and test coverage as separate reviewer passes.
  These can be ephemeral (fresh agent per round).
- **Synthesise**: reconcile the reviewers' findings into one set of required changes.
- **Pass? gate**: if synthesised feedback has no blocking issues, finalize and commit that unit
  with its own commit message, then move to the next planned unit. If it fails, send the
  synthesised feedback back to the Worker as another round on the same unit (don't restart from
  the Planner unless the feedback reveals the plan itself was wrong).

Net effect: one commit per feature/unit, each vetted by multiple reviewer passes before it lands,
rather than a single large uncommitted or unreviewed diff at the end.

## Verifying UI work: visual recreation (the main way to verify)

For any unit that changes UI, the primary verification is a **visual recreation**: render the real
components with mock data and look at a screenshot. Typecheck and unit tests are necessary but do not
count as verifying how it looks. Workers should do this before reporting, and I re-do it (or open the
image for the user) when the user asks to see it.

1. Add a **temporary** preview route (e.g. `apps/web/app/zz-preview/page.tsx`) that imports the real
   components and renders them with realistic mock props: populated, empty, capped/failed, long
   names/links. Put context around them (page background, a mock frame for panels/drawers that need a
   session or client state) but never reimplement the component itself.
2. Start the dev server in the background with dummy env vars the app needs to boot (e.g.
   `CONVEX_URL=https://dummy.convex.cloud CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY=x NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 bunx next dev -p <port>`),
   wait for "Ready", and `curl` the route for a 200.
3. Screenshot with headless Chrome, not the preview MCP tools (those time out):
   `"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless=new --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --force-device-scale-factor=2 --virtual-time-budget=6000 --window-size=<w>,<h> --screenshot=/tmp/<name>.png <url>`
   Take a wide desktop shot and a narrow one. Headless Chrome enforces a minimum window width, so a
   narrow shot can come out horizontally clipped; for true 320px checks render inside a 320px-wide
   iframe or measure element widths, and say so rather than treating clipping as a bug.
4. **Read the PNG** (the Read tool shows images) and actually look at it: hierarchy, spacing, truncation,
   overflow, alignment, tap targets, copy. Report what was seen versus what was not verified
   (hover/focus states, real clipboard/share, animations, Safari-only behavior, the real page behind auth).
5. For the user, `open` the desktop screenshot (copy it to `~/Downloads/<name>.png` first) since they
   can't see tool-output images.
6. **Clean up before committing**: stop the dev server (`pkill -f "next dev -p <port>"`), delete the
   preview route, temp public files and stray `.next` artifacts, and confirm `git status` shows only
   intended changes. Never commit a preview route or mocks.

# Mandatory visual + local-server verification (every agent, every run)

Applies to any task that changes code a user can see or that the running app depends on. No unit of
work is "done" until both of these have happened and been reported:

1. **Run it against the local server.** Start the real dev server (and `npx convex dev` when Convex
   code changed) in this worktree, wait for "Ready", and exercise the changed path end to end: `curl`
   the route for the expected status and hit changed API routes. A passing typecheck/lint/build alone
   does not count.
2. **Verify visually with a screenshot.** Follow the visual-recreation steps above (headless Chrome,
   wide + narrow shot), then Read the PNG and look at it. For pages behind auth, use a temporary
   preview route with mock data. Non-UI changes still get a screenshot of the affected page to prove
   nothing regressed.
3. **Report** what was seen, what was not verified (hover/focus, auth-gated pages, animations), and
   the screenshot path. If the server can't boot (e.g. missing env vars), say so explicitly and fix
   the env first (see below); never claim success without having run it.
4. Clean up (stop the server, delete preview routes/temp files) before committing.

Env vars: each worktree needs its own copy of the gitignored `.env*` files. If `.env.local` is
missing in the current worktree, symlink it from the canonical copy at `~/.config/avian/.env.local`
(`ln -s ~/.config/avian/.env.local .env.local`) before starting the server.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# AgentBisect `git bisect` for agent behavior. Give it a failing agent run (or just a known-good and known-bad commit). It finds the commit that broke the behavior, explains why that commit was written, and proves the culprit by reverting it. Built for neatHack (Oct 10, 2026). Business case: [AgentBisect financial model on CFO.ai](https://cfo.ai/s/nx6S-5QNKtJFVkRp) (spreadsheet copy: [`evidence/cfo-ai/`](evidence/cfo-ai/)). > Every figure below is copied from a file in `evidence/` (final re-run: [`evidence/rerun3-summary.md`](evidence/rerun3-summary.md)). > Open the HTML reports with `open evidence/report-.html`; `evidence/dogfooding.md` covers using AgentBisect on its own build. ## What it is Agents regress in ways unit tests do not catch: a refactor changes the unit of a refund amount, a "helpful" change makes the agent cancel orders nobody asked to cancel, a new tool schema quietly doubles token spend. `git bisect` can find the commit, but it needs a deterministic good/bad test, and an LLM agent gives you a noisy one. AgentBisect supplies that test. It runs the target repo's eval suite at each commit it probes, in an isolated git worktree, with repeats and a calibrated baseline so a flaky run is not mistaken for a regression. Then it bisects. The demo target is [`support-agent-demo`](https://github.com/jaxsonsprinkles/support-agent-demo): a customer-support agent (pinned Haiku) with mocked tools, 24 eval cases at HEAD (18 exist at the good commit), and a seeded history of regressions written by a separate coding-agent session. ## How it works 1. **Intake.** Start from a neatlogs trace, a neatlogs detection, or a GitHub issue. Intake maps it to an eval case, finds a known-good commit (an earlier passing run of the same case), and records a `RegressionSpec`. 2. **Failure signatures.** At the bad end, every distinct failing check (for example `call_args:issue_refund.amount`, `must_not_call`, `budget:tokens@order_status`) becomes its own *signature*, and each is bisected separately. One range can hide several regressions; bisecting "the suite fails" would blame whichever commit lands last. A signature that also fails at the good end is a known pre-existing failure, and AgentBisect refuses to bisect it instead of inventing a culprit. 3. **Plain bisect.** Classic binary search over `git rev-list --first-parent`, with a monotonic probe after convergence that flags "multiple regressions likely" when the history is not clean good-then-bad. 4. **Smart (weighted) bisect.** A planner ranks the commits in range by how likely each is to be the culprit, then picks the next commit by weighted bisection (split the probability mass, not the commit count) and falls back to plain when the ranking is uninformative. Signals, in order: - **Span divergence**: where the bad run first differs from a good run (a different tool, different arguments, an extra step). See [span divergence](#span-divergence-and-the-fixture-fallback). - **Code impact**: `entire graph impact` finds which commits touched the code behind the divergent tool. - **Entire intent**: each candidate's [Entire](https://entire.io) checkpoint (the prompt and reasoning of the coding session that wrote it). Commits that were *meant* to change the failing area rank higher. 5. **Median budget checks.** Token and step regressions are judged against a per-case **median** from a one-time calibration run at the good commit (`agentbisect calibrate`), never recalibrated mid-investigation. A run is over budget past 1.5x the case median. Medians, not means, so one slow sample does not move the line. 6. **Verifier (revert test).** The culp ... [6742 characters truncated] ... : step 1: bad run made an extra step search_help ``` The fixture is the tool-call sequence of case `os1` ("Where is order 1042?") at `1b40b27` and `0ecffc0`, taken from real `python -m evals run --json` output (Haiku through the llm-proxy). It is always labelled as a fixture, never presented as live neatlogs data. The bad commit is the tip of the range, so the fixture shows where behavior changed (an extra `search_help` step), not which commit caused it. It contains tool-call spans only; model-call spans are not in the runner's report. `agentbisect.fixtures.FixtureDirSource` plugs into the same `TraceSource` interface as the live source, and `--bundle OUT.json` writes the single-file form that `--fixtures` accepts. `record_pair` records new fixtures from two eval reports. ## Next steps These are the next steps for what we're going to tackle next with AgentBisect. Each one comes from something the evidence showed us. - **Unblock neatlogs span divergence.** Multi-span traces currently dead-letter (`finalizationStatus: "dlq"`, `spansCount: 0`), even for a bare two-span script with no model calls, and the SDK reports zero export failures. The trace ids are in [`evidence/neatlogs-dlq-report.md`](evidence/neatlogs-dlq-report.md). Once traces finalize, we'll run the planner on live span divergence instead of the recorded fixture (the final re-run ranked on code impact and checkpoint intent only), and verify `NeatlogsCliSource.spans` against the real span shape, since it was written against the documented CLI. - **Make token-budget signatures reliable.** Every token regression (a new tool schema, an extra "verify with search" rule) inflates every category, so a per-category budget signature tends to blame whichever commit crosses 1.5x last, and its revert test can fail with "multiple regressions likely". Behavioural signatures (wrong arguments, forbidden tool calls) are already far more reliable. We'll attribute token growth per commit rather than per threshold crossing; a tool-count signal for token signatures is on an unmerged branch. Per-signature outcomes are in `evidence/rerun3-summary.md` (4 of 6 correct on the final re-run). - **Make smart bisect cheaper on budget signatures.** It already uses fewer eval rounds than plain on behavioural signatures (18 vs 24, 3 vs 4), but more on budget signatures (96 vs 84, 60 vs 54). We'll improve the ranking there, and repeat the planner-context saving on more than one investigation and range. - **Tighten the noisy "bad" judgement.** Haiku at non-zero temperature (the proxy cannot set it) is stochastic. Repeats, medians and a confidence band reduce that noise; we want to cut it further, and keep labelling low-confidence culprits as such. - **Measure context savings properly.** The current token counts are bytes/4 estimates, and the "without graph" side is an estimate rather than a second run. We'll replace both with real token counts from actual runs. - **Broaden the Fixer and Verifier evidence.** So far it is one run per configuration, one culprit (R3), six runs in total, about $0.9 of model calls, and the one VERIFIED result is an eval-expectation update, not a code fix. We'll run more culprits and more samples, and get a real code fix through the Verifier. - **Make eval-expectation edits safer.** The Fixer's checks run the fix commit's own cases file, so an edited expectation is what they see; the Verifier flags the change rather than re-running against the old expectation. # AgentBisect `git bisect` for agent behavior. Give it a failing agent run (or just a known-good and known-bad commit). It finds the commit that broke the behavior, explains why that commit was written, and proves the culprit by reverting it. Built for neatHack (Oct 10, 2026). AgentBisect supplies that test. It runs the target repo's eval suite at each commit it probes, in an isolated git worktree, with repeats and a calibrated baseline so a flaky run is not mistaken for a regression. Then it bisects. The demo target is [`support-agent-demo`](https://github.com/jaxsonsprinkles/support-agent-demo): a customer-support agent (pinned Haiku) with mocked tools, 24 eval cases at HEAD (18 exist at the good commit), and a seeded history of regressions written by a separate coding-agent session. ## How it works 1. **Intake.** Start from a neatlogs trace, a neatlogs detection, or a GitHub issue. One range can hide several regressions; bisecting "the suite fails" would blame whichever commit lands last. A signature that also fails at the good end is a known pre-existing failure, and AgentBisect refuses to bisect it instead of inventing a culprit. 3. **Plain bisect.** Classic binary search over `git rev-list --first-parent`, with a monotonic probe after convergence that flags "multiple regressions likely" when the history is not clean good-then-bad. 4. **Smart (weighted) bisect.** A planner ranks the commits in range by how likely each is to be the culprit, then picks the next commit by weighted bisection (split the probability mass, not the commit count) and falls back to plain when the ranking is uninformative. 5. **Median budget checks.** Token and step regressions are judged against a per-case **median** from a one-time calibration run at the good commit (`agentbisect calibrate`), never recalibrated mid-investigation. A run is over budget past 1.5x the case median. Medians, not means, so one slow sample does not move the line.
6. **Verifier (revert test).** The culprit is only reported with confidence if reverting it at the bad end flips the signature from failing to passing (before and after pass rates are recorded). Revert conflicts, partial reverts and unbuildable trees lower confidence or end as `inconclusive`.
7. **Explain.** The culprit report quotes the Entire checkpoint (why the commit was written), the semantic diff, and the first span divergence, so the answer is "this commit, written to do X, causes Y", not just a SHA.
8. **Fixer.** A fresh agent that sees only the culprit diff, the stated intent, and the failing evidence (never the planted-regression metadata) proposes a fix that keeps the intent, up to 3 attempts. An intent check runs inside the Fixer, so "revert the culprit" does not pass. Where the culprit *deliberately* changed a contract and the eval expectations are stale, the Fixer may update those expectations, narrowly and only for cases sharing the target's check; every such change is recorded and flagged "human review required". `report --open-pr` and `fix --open-draft-pr` are dry runs by default and push nothing without explicit confirmation.
9. **Fix Verifier.** `agentbisect verify-fix` re-checks the fix commit on four counts: the target signature no longer reproduces, the regression suite still passes, held-out cases pass (the fix is not overfit), and a pinned intent judge says the culprit's intent survives. Any failure is NOT VERIFIED; a judge outage or missing held-out cases is inconclusive, never a pass.

Roles, model pins and isolation rules are in [`ROLES.md`](ROLES.md). The agent and judge models are pinned and recorded in every result, and results produced under different pins are never mixed.

### Fixer and Verifier: live results

Run six times live on the R3 refund-amount culprit `b0be626` ([`evidence/fix-demo/README.md`](evidence/fix-demo/README.md)). Run 6 is **VERIFIED**: target pass, regression 13/13, held-out 1.00 (with 1 held-out expectation change), intent judge pass. Read what the fix is: **it changes no code.** The culprit deliberately moved `issue_refund` to integer cents, so the eval expectations were stale; the fix updates 4 eval expectations (rw1-rw3 target, rw4 held-out), all flagged for human review. A person should confirm that is the intended resolution.

The earlier runs are the interesting part: the Fixer reverted the culprit and passed its own checks (the intent judge caught it), frozen evals made any fix impossible, and two bugs in our own guards turned up live. Each led to a change. 326 tests pass.

| What | Result | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Planner context with the Entire graph vs reading the raw range | 12,869 vs 26,420 tokens (51.3% cut). Measured on investigation `6857f0b738`, a different range from the final re-run | [`evidence/entire-context-savings.md`](evidence/entire-context-savings.md) |
| Signatures correct on the full-range re-run (good `1b40b27`, bad `0ecffc0`) | 4 of 6 | [`evidence/rerun3-summary.md`](evidence/rerun3-summary.md) |
| Revert tests | 2 passed, 2 failed, 1 inconclusive; the sixth signature (es2) was correctly refused as a pre-existing failure, so none was run | same |
| Eval rounds, plain vs smart | 24 vs 18, 4 vs 3, 84 vs 96, 54 vs 60, 21 vs 21. Smart won on the two behavioural signatures and lost on budget signatures (84 vs 96, 54 vs 60), tied on one (21 vs 21) | same |

`agentbisect summary <state_dir> --format md` regenerates the per-signature table from saved state.

## Setup

Requirements: Python 3.11 to 3.13 (the neatlogs SDK does not support 3.14), [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), `git`, and for the full pipeline the `entire` CLI with the `graph` plugin.

```bash
uv sync
cp .env.example .env     # NEATLOGS_API_KEY, NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID, ...
uv run pytest -q         # fake executors and throwaway git repos; no model or network calls
```

The target repo needs `evals/cases.jsonl` and the eval CLI contract (`python -m evals run --json --isolate ...`, schema version 1) described in the `support-agent-demo` repo. Clone it next to this one.

Optional pieces:

- **neatlogs CLI** (`npm i -g --prefix ~/.local/neatlogs-cli neatlogs-cli`) for live trace intake, after a one-time `auth login --device`. See `hackathon.md`.
- **Entire** (`entire enable` in the target repo; `entire plugin install graph`) for checkpoint intent and code impact. Without it the planner falls back to commit messages and plain bisect.
- **LLM backend.** Either set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or run on your own logged-in `claude` CLI with `--llm-proxy auto` (personal use, your own login only; see `ROLES.md`). The proxy cannot set temperature, so repeats absorb the extra noise.

## Usage

```bash
# 1. Calibrate the token baseline once, at the known-good commit
uv run agentbisect calibrate --repo ../support-agent-demo --good 1b40b27 --llm-proxy auto

# 2. Investigate from a bad trace (or --detection ID, or --issue URL)

`agentbisect summary <state_dir> --format md` regenerates the per-signature table from saved state.

## Setup

Requirements: Python 3.11 to 3.13 (the neatlogs SDK does not support 3.14), [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), `git`, and for the full pipeline the `entire` CLI with the `graph` plugin.

```bash
uv sync
cp .env.example .env     # NEATLOGS_API_KEY, NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID, ...
uv run pytest -q         # fake executors and throwaway git repos; no model or network calls
```

The target repo needs `evals/cases.jsonl` and the eval CLI contract (`python -m evals run --json --isolate ...`, schema version 1) described in the `support-agent-demo` repo. Clone it next to this one.

Optional pieces:

- **neatlogs CLI** (`npm i -g --prefix ~/.local/neatlogs-cli neatlogs-cli`) for live trace intake, after a one-time `auth login --device`. See `hackathon.md`.
- **Entire** (`entire enable` in the target repo; `entire plugin install graph`) for checkpoint intent and code impact. Without it the planner falls back to commit messages and plain bisect.
- **LLM backend.** Either set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or run on your own logged-in `claude` CLI with `--llm-proxy auto` (personal use, your own login only; see `ROLES.md`). The proxy cannot set temperature, so repeats absorb the extra noise.

## Usage

```bash
# 1. Calibrate the token baseline once, at the known-good commit
uv run agentbisect calibrate --repo ../support-agent-demo --good 1b40b27 --llm-proxy auto

# 2. Investigate from a bad trace (or --detection ID, or --issue URL)

Welcome to BoardUI — a React + Tailwind CSS v4 design system with agent-first tooling.

BoardUI is a React + Tailwind CSS v4 design system (Next.js first) with free components and paid Pro components/templates. This server installs component source directly into the user's project — no terminal needed.

Typical flow:
1. In a project without BoardUI, call init_boardui once (installs Tailwind v4 + runtime deps, writes styles/ and utils/).
2. Discover with list_components; read source/props with get_component; get working code with get_usage_examples.
3. Install with install_components — it writes the files and installs npm deps.

Component names are exact — when unsure, call list_components instead of guessing.

## RTL Support

BoardUI supports Arabic, Hebrew, and other right-to-left languages across free components, Pro blocks, and templates. The same source handles RTL and LTR; there is no RTL CLI flag or separate component version.

1. Read get_component and get_usage_examples for the free `direction` item. Install it with install_components (stdio), or write its source and dependencies yourself (read-only HTTP). CLI equivalent: `npx boardui@latest add direction`.
2. Wrap the app with DirectionProvider using an explicit BCP 47 locale: `ar` for Arabic, `he` for Hebrew, `en-US` for English. Set matching `lang` and `dir` on `<html>` for a full-app RTL layout. CSS dir alone does not configure React Aria keyboard navigation, calendars, or portalled menus.

```tsx
import { DirectionProvider } from "@/components/foundations/direction/direction";

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="ar" dir="rtl">
      <body>
        <DirectionProvider locale="ar">{children}</DirectionProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

3. Use logical styles such as ps/pe, ms/me, start/end, and text-start/text-end. Mirror navigation arrows and drawer motion; preserve physical coordinates for charts, canvas, and decorative art. Custom portals should carry `dir={useDirection()}` on their root. Nest DirectionProvider for mixed-language regions.
4. Keep email addresses, URLs, OTP digits, and code LTR; isolate mixed text with bdi or dir=auto. Choose fonts with Arabic or Hebrew coverage and avoid extra letter spacing for Arabic. Translate application labels and accessible names in the application's translation layer; use Intl for dates, numbers, and currencies. Optional `template-copy` supplies TemplateCopyProvider for translating template display copy. Chinese (`zh-CN`) remains LTR.
5. For older installations, refresh the provider, component source, shared dependencies, and global styles. Preserve customizations before using overwrite. Pro updates use the licensed CLI or updated source downloads.

Setup and live Arabic/Hebrew examples: https://www.boardui.com/rtl

Design rules (always apply when writing UI in a BoardUI project): style with BoardUI's semantic Tailwind tokens, never raw palette classes or hex — text via text-text-primary/-secondary/-tertiary, surfaces via bg-background-*-default/-hover, borders via border-border-* and border-separator-border, icons via text-foreground-icon-*. Type uses composite utilities (text-title-2-medium, text-headline-medium, text-body-medium, ...) that set size/weight/line-height together — never rebuild them from text-sm font-medium. Dark mode flips tokens automatically via the .dark class; never hardcode dark: colors. Merge classes with cx() from @/utils/cx (or the utils alias configured in boardui.json); icons from @remixicon/react as component references. init_boardui installs these rules as always-on files (AGENTS.md + .cursor/rules/boardui.mdc) so they survive beyond this session; install_rules adds them to an already initialized project.

Monorepos/custom aliases: put boardui.json next to the destination package's package.json, and pass that package as projectDir. Installs read its paths/aliases and keep npm dependencies in that package. Pass projectDir to get_component and get_usage_examples too for matching source and examples. Package exports and each consuming app's stylesheet/Tailwind setup must already be wired by the project.

Agent skill: BoardUI also ships an agent skill (SKILL.md open standard) carrying deeper always-loaded knowledge — the full component catalog, theming, page patterns, and the motion language. get_skill answers questions about it (returns SKILL.md and the file list); install_skill writes it into the project's .claude/skills/boardui. For other destinations, relay the CLI: npx boardui@latest skill (project), --global (~/.claude/skills), --client codex (~/.agents/skills, read by Codex and Gemini), --path <dir> (anywhere), --force (update). Docs: https://www.boardui.com/skill

Pro: items marked PRO require a one-time BoardUI Pro license (https://www.boardui.com/pricing, lifetime updates). If the user wants a pro item and no license is active, relay the pricing link — and if they already purchased, ask them for the license key from their purchase email, then call activate_license with it. After that, pro installs work like free ones.

Pro license on this machine: none yet — pro items show a purchase link (https://www.boardui.com/pricing).

Tools: list_components, get_component, get_usage_examples, install_components, init_boardui, install_rules, get_skill, install_skill, get_theme, activate_license, license_status, deactivate_license.

<!-- boardui:rules:start -->
# BoardUI design rules

This project uses BoardUI (React + Tailwind CSS v4, source-owned components under `components/`). These rules always apply when writing UI code. MCP tools are on demand; these rules are not optional context.

## Components first

- Before hand-building any UI element, check for an installed BoardUI component under `components/base/` and `components/application/`, and prefer it.
- Missing a component? Install it (BoardUI MCP `install_components`, or `npx boardui@latest add <name>`) instead of writing a lookalike.
- Import through the `@/` alias, e.g. `import { Button } from "@/components/base/buttons/button"`.

## Color: semantic tokens only

- Never use raw palette classes (`text-gray-500`, `bg-white`, `border-neutral-200`) or hex/oklch literals. Every color rides a BoardUI semantic token, which also makes dark mode automatic.
- Text: `text-text-primary`, `text-text-secondary`, `text-text-tertiary`, `text-text-placeholder`, errors `text-text-error-primary`.
- Surfaces: `bg-background-primary-default`, `bg-background-secondary-default` / `-hover`, `bg-background-tertiary-default`, page ground `bg-background-full`.
- Borders: `border-border-button-default` / `-hover`, hairlines `border-separator-border`, tables `border-border-table`, errors `border-border-error-default`.
- Icons: `text-foreground-icon-primary` through `text-foreground-icon-quaternary`.
- Charts: the `chart-1` … `chart-5` tokens (plus `-active` variants). CTAs and selection states: the `accent-50` … `accent-950` ramp.
- Dark mode flips tokens via the `.dark` class on `<html>`. Do not write `dark:` overrides with raw colors; if a token pair looks wrong in dark mode, pick a different token, not a literal.

## Typography: composite utilities only

- Use BoardUI's composite type utilities: `text-title-1-medium`, `text-title-2-medium`, `text-title-3-semibold`, `text-headline-medium`, `text-body-medium`, `text-body-regular`, `text-body-2-*`, `text-caption-1-semibold`, and friends. Each sets size, weight, line-height, and letter-spacing together.
- Never rebuild type by stacking `text-sm font-medium leading-5`; if a style seems missing, look in `styles/typography.css` before inventing one.

## Spacing and shape

- Stay on Tailwind's spacing scale (`gap-2`, `p-4`, `mt-6`); prefer flex/grid `gap` over per-child margins. Arbitrary values (`p-[13px]`) only when matching an existing BoardUI component exactly.
- Cards and panels: `rounded-3xl` with `border-border-button-default`. Inputs and menu rows: `rounded-md` to `rounded-xl`. Pills: `rounded-full`.

## Mechanics

- Direction: wrap the app (or a mixed-language region) in `DirectionProvider` from `@/components/foundations/direction/direction`, with an explicit BCP 47 `locale` (`ar`, `he`, `en-US`, `zh-CN`). Set matching `lang` and `dir` on `<html>` for full-app RTL. CSS `dir` alone does not configure React Aria keyboard navigation or portal placement. Use `useDirection()` for custom interactions and put its value on custom portal roots.
- Use logical styles: `ms`/`me`, `ps`/`pe`, `start`/`end`, `text-start`/`text-end`, `border-s`/`border-e`, `rounded-s`/`rounded-e`, and inline logical CSS properties. Mirror navigation/disclosure glyphs and horizontal drawer motion in RTL. Preserve physical coordinates for measured geometry, charts, canvas, and decorative art. Keep code, OTP digits, email addresses and URLs in explicit LTR regions; isolate mixed text with `<bdi>` or `dir="auto"`. Translating labels and formatting application data is separate from layout direction. See https://www.boardui.com/rtl.

- Internal vertical scroll regions must soften the top edge with a progressive blur and surface fade once scrolled, rather than sharply clipping content. Keep headers outside the scroll region. Use a stationary, `pointer-events-none`, `aria-hidden` overlay in a relative wrapper: a 24px masked 1px backdrop blur, a 16px masked 4px backdrop blur, and a gradient from the enclosing semantic surface token to transparent. Ramp each layer's opacity from 0 to 1 over the first 24px of scrolling; keep it invisible at scrollTop 0. Apply opacity to the individual layers, never the overlay parent (a translucent parent creates a backdrop root and can break blur at normal browser zoom). Verify top/reset, overflow, light/dark mode, and 100% zoom; preserve keyboard scrolling and do not blur the whole content area.

- Merge classes with `cx()` from `@/utils/cx` (tailwind-merge aware of BoardUI's composite text styles). No string concatenation, no plain `clsx`.
- Icons come from `@remixicon/react`, passed as component references (`leadingIcon={RiAddLine}`), not rendered elements.
- Form components build on `react-aria-components`; extend the installed BoardUI form components rather than raw `<input>`/`<select>`.
- Focus states: `outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring`.

When unsure about a token, a component's API, or working example code, ask the BoardUI MCP server: `get_theme`, `get_component`, `get_usage_examples`.
<!-- boardui:rules:end -->

<!-- boardui:rules:start -->
# BoardUI design rules

This project uses BoardUI (React + Tailwind CSS v4, source-owned components under `components/`). These rules always apply when writing UI code. MCP tools are on demand; these rules are not optional context.

## Components first

- Before hand-building any UI element, check for an installed BoardUI component under `components/base/` and `components/application/`, and prefer it.
- Missing a component? Install it (BoardUI MCP `install_components`, or `npx boardui@latest add <name>`) instead of writing a lookalike.
- Import through the `@/` alias, e.g. `import { Button } from "@/components/base/buttons/button"`.

## Color: semantic tokens only

- Never use raw palette classes (`text-gray-500`, `bg-white`, `border-neutral-200`) or hex/oklch literals. Every color rides a BoardUI semantic token, which also makes dark mode automatic.
- Text: `text-text-primary`, `text-text-secondary`, `text-text-tertiary`, `text-text-placeholder`, errors `text-text-error-primary`.
- Surfaces: `bg-background-primary-default`, `bg-background-secondary-default` / `-hover`, `bg-background-tertiary-default`, page ground `bg-background-full`.
- Borders: `border-border-button-default` / `-hover`, hairlines `border-separator-border`, tables `border-border-table`, errors `border-border-error-default`.
- Icons: `text-foreground-icon-primary` through `text-foreground-icon-quaternary`.
- Charts: the `chart-1` … `chart-5` tokens (plus `-active` variants). CTAs and selection states: the `accent-50` … `accent-950` ramp.
- Dark mode flips tokens via the `.dark` class on `<html>`. Do not write `dark:` overrides with raw colors; if a token pair looks wrong in dark mode, pick a different token, not a literal.

## Typography: composite utilities only

- Use BoardUI's composite type utilities: `text-title-1-medium`, `text-title-2-medium`, `text-title-3-semibold`, `text-headline-medium`, `text-body-medium`, `text-body-regular`, `text-body-2-*`, `text-caption-1-semibold`, and friends. Each sets size, weight, line-height, and letter-spacing together.
- Never rebuild type by stacking `text-sm font-medium leading-5`; if a style seems missing, look in `styles/typography.css` before inventing one.

## Spacing and shape

- Stay on Tailwind's spacing scale (`gap-2`, `p-4`, `mt-6`); prefer flex/grid `gap` over per-child margins. Arbitrary values (`p-[13px]`) only when matching an existing BoardUI component exactly.
- Cards and panels: `rounded-3xl` with `border-border-button-default`. Inputs and menu rows: `rounded-md` to `rounded-xl`. Pills: `rounded-full`.

## Mechanics

- Direction: wrap the app (or a mixed-language region) in `DirectionProvider` from `@/components/foundations/direction/direction`, with an explicit BCP 47 `locale` (`ar`, `he`, `en-US`, `zh-CN`). Set matching `lang` and `dir` on `<html>` for full-app RTL. CSS `dir` alone does not configure React Aria keyboard navigation or portal placement. Use `useDirection()` for custom interactions and put its value on custom portal roots.
- Use logical styles: `ms`/`me`, `ps`/`pe`, `start`/`end`, `text-start`/`text-end`, `border-s`/`border-e`, `rounded-s`/`rounded-e`, and inline logical CSS properties. Mirror navigation/disclosure glyphs and horizontal drawer motion in RTL. Preserve physical coordinates for measured geometry, charts, canvas, and decorative art. Keep code, OTP digits, email addresses and URLs in explicit LTR regions; isolate mixed text with `<bdi>` or `dir="auto"`. Translating labels and formatting application data is separate from layout direction. See https://www.boardui.com/rtl.

- Internal vertical scroll regions must soften the top edge with a progressive blur and surface fade once scrolled, rather than sharply clipping content. Keep headers outside the scroll region. Use a stationary, `pointer-events-none`, `aria-hidden` overlay in a relative wrapper: a 24px masked 1px backdrop blur, a 16px masked 4px backdrop blur, and a gradient from the enclosing semantic surface token to transparent. Ramp each layer's opacity from 0 to 1 over the first 24px of scrolling; keep it invisible at scrollTop 0. Apply opacity to the individual layers, never the overlay parent (a translucent parent creates a backdrop root and can break blur at normal browser zoom). Verify top/reset, overflow, light/dark mode, and 100% zoom; preserve keyboard scrolling and do not blur the whole content area.

- Merge classes with `cx()` from `@/utils/cx` (tailwind-merge aware of BoardUI's composite text styles). No string concatenation, no plain `clsx`.
- Icons come from `@remixicon/react`, passed as component references (`leadingIcon={RiAddLine}`), not rendered elements.
- Form components build on `react-aria-components`; extend the installed BoardUI form components rather than raw `<input>`/`<select>`.
- Focus states: `outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-focus-ring`.

When unsure about a token, a component's API, or working example code, ask the BoardUI MCP server: `get_theme`, `get_component`, `get_usage_examples`.
<!-- boardui:rules:end -->

content.text:
## Base components (free)
- tree-view: Nested folders and structured content with expandable branches, selection, guide lines, and keyboard navigation.
- button: Primary, secondary, ghost, and danger buttons in three sizes with icon support.
- icon-button: Square icon-only button in two sizes.
- link-button: Inline text action styled like a link — primary/secondary variants, three sizes, icon support, renders <a> or <button>.
- button-group: Row of secondary-style buttons fused into one bordered control with hairline dividers and selectable items.
- close-button: Compact dismiss button for banners, modals, and chips.
- input: Text input with label, hint text, error states, and leading icon support.
- textarea: Multiline text field with auto-grow, character count, and Input's label, hint and states.
- checkbox: React Aria checkbox with animated tick and indeterminate state.
- checkbox-card: Bordered selectable card driven by a checkbox.
- radio: React Aria radio group with the gradient selected dot, two sizes, and the bare RadioDot glyph for menu rows.
- radio-card: Bordered selectable card driven by a radio — the radio flavor of Checkbox Card.
- switch: Skeuomorphic toggle switch in two sizes.
- switch-card: Bordered settings row driven by a switch.
- select: React Aria select with styled trigger, non-modal popover, and free-form item content.
- slider: Single-value and min/max range sliders with exact-value bubbles and keyboard controls.
- social-button: Sign-in buttons for 24 providers, with brand logos, three colour treatments and an icon-only form.
- dropdown: Composable popover menu (trigger, panel, groups, rows, dividers) built on React Aria — the recipe behind the sidebar team/account menus.
- divider: Horizontal content divider with single-line, double-line, filled, and aligned variants.
- file-upload: Drag-and-drop file upload with validation, animated progress, and a completion callback.
- tabs: Underline and pill tab variants built on React Aria.
- table: Static table primitives matching the dashboard tables.
- tooltip: Light-surface tooltip built on React Aria.
- badge: Counter pills and the Kbd shortcut hint.
- chip: Status/delta chips in bold and soft variants across the accent palette.
- status-dot: Colored status indicator dot used inside selects and tables.
- avatar: Image or initials avatar in multiple sizes and tints.
- breadcrumb: Icon-capable breadcrumb trail.
- pagination: Numbered pagination with prev/next and ellipsis collapsing.
- carousel: Gallery carousel built on CSS scroll-snap: swipe, arrows and a position indicator.
- input-otp: One-time-code field with a monospace box per digit, paste distribution and autofill support.
- segmented-control: Pill-style segmented control (Weekly / Monthly / Yearly switchers).
- announcement: Dismissible announcement card used in the sidebar footer.
- notification: Dismissible notification with status icons, avatars, action buttons, and timed countdown.
- kbd: Keyboard shortcut hint pill.
- date-picker: Single-date picker with month navigation, built on React Aria.
- date-range-picker: Two-month range picker sharing the date-picker chrome.
- meeting-scheduler: Date + time-slot scheduler popover.

## Application blocks (free)
- theme-toggle: Manual light/dark control with a click-origin reveal, local persistence, and no system-theme dependency.
- agent-chat: A working chat app: app sidebar, streaming replies, thinking indicator, a composer pill with stop control, a chat-history rail with local thread switching, and a setup notice when no provider key is set.
- app-shell: Page frame for the chat starter: the sidebar, a phone drawer, and a titled content card, carrying the starter's own navigation so the sidebar only links to pages the app has.
- agent-thinking: Agent thinking indicator for chat composers — dot wave, dot spin, stars, and infinity variants with a shimmering label and elapsed timer.
- agent-log: Shared streaming-log machinery: the reveal ticker, the blur-in with its soft clipping edge, and the curved tree guide that draws itself. Behind Task List and Web Search.
- composer-loader: Loading state that wraps a chat composer — an iridescent light band orbiting the rim with a soft inward bloom, fading in while the agent works.
- sidebar: The floating dashboard sidebar with team menu, nav, announcement, and user menu.
- settings-modal: Controlled multi-page settings dialog with General, Profile, Tools, and Storage views.
- auth-card: Sign-in and sign-up cards with social providers stacked with labels or inline as icons, plus email fields and a CTA.
- notification-center: Tabbed activity inbox with grouped notifications, unread state, avatars, status icons, and inline actions.
- data-grid: Virtualized spreadsheet with editable cells, range selection, filters, resizable columns, undo and redo, summaries, and CSV export.
- data-table: TanStack-powered data table with sorting, selection, and pagination.
- stat-cards: KPI stat card row with delta chips.
- revenue-chart-card: Free chart card: a year of monthly revenue as an area against the year before, with a count-up headline, delta chip and hover readout per month.
- orders-chart-card: Free chart card: a year of monthly orders as bars, this year beside last year for every month, with a count-up headline, delta chip and hover readout.
- important-alerts-card: Scrollable alert feed with tinted icon circles and date pills.
- patient-info-card: Profile card with avatar and label/value detail rows.

## Foundations (free)
- template-copy: Optional application translations for template labels, sample content, and accessible names, preserving identifiers and input values.
- direction: Locale and layout direction for RTL and LTR regions, React Aria interactions, and portals.
- scroll-direction: Logical horizontal scroll offsets and item alignment for RTL and LTR carousels and tab strips.
- directional-icon: Mirrors navigation arrows and sidebar glyphs in RTL while preserving non-directional icons.
- theme: Color primitives, semantic tokens (text/background/border/foreground/chart), radii, shadows, and button gradient utilities.
- typography: The full Figma type scale as composite text-{family}-{weight} Tailwind utilities.
- globals: Tailwind entry css: dark-mode variant, base resets, component animations, and table styling. Imports theme.css and typography.css.
- cx: tailwind-merge wrapper aware of BoardUI's composite text styles, plus the sortCx helper.
- rules: Always-on design rules for AI agents (semantic tokens, type scale, conventions), installed as a Cursor rule file.
- use-dismiss-on-outside-press: Closes React Aria popovers on outside press without swallowing the outside click.
- use-count-up: Animated rolling number hook used by chart headline figures.
- chevrons: Custom chevron glyphs (select caret, sortable table headers) matching the Figma strokes.
- logo: BoardUI brand mark placeholder — swap with your own logo component.
- agent-runtime: Streaming chat endpoint for agent templates: one AI_API_KEY from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter, Groq, xAI or Vercel AI Gateway (or any OpenAI-compatible server by URL), a config probe for unconfigured deploys, and the message contract the BoardUI chat UI installs against.

Next: get_component for source + props, get_usage_examples for working snippets, install_components to add to the project.

# Re-run 3: calibrated baseline, median budgets, refusal, full range to 0ecffc0

Target support-agent-demo, good `1b40b27`, bad `0ecffc0`, started from the rw1 trace e2dad535 (`--good 1b40b27 --bad 0ecffc0`).
DEMO_FLAKE=0, agent claude-haiku-5-5, judge claude-sonnet-5-5, llm-proxy on the logged-in `claude` CLI (concurrency 4).
Steps: one `calibrate` at 1b40b27 (`baseline-1b40b27.json`, never recalibrated), `investigate --strategy smart --all-signatures
--all-categories` (budget 3 repeats, behavioural 1), then `compare` per signature. State and logs: `rerun3-smart/`, `rerun3-compare/`.

| signature | culprit found | revert test (before -> after) | plain vs smart rounds | vs private key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| call_args:issue_refund.amount | b0be626 (medium) | PASSED, pass 0% -> 100% | 24 vs 18 | correct |
| must_not_call (proactive cancel_order) | 0ecffc0 (high) | PASSED, pass 0% -> 100% | 4 vs 3 | correct |
| budget:tokens@order_status | 59c8b10 (low) | FAILED, median tokens 20,405 -> 22,861 (good 8,866), within budget 0/4 -> 0/4 | 84 vs 96 | incorrect |
| budget:tokens@refund_within_policy | 59c8b10 (low) | FAILED, median tokens 39,306 -> 35,195, within budget 0/3 -> 0/3 | 54 vs 60 | correct (mixed signal) |
| budget:tokens@refund_outside_policy | 5cee99b (medium) | inconclusive | 21 vs 21 | incorrect |
| call_args:escalate_to_human.priority (es2) | none: known pre-existing failure, correctly refused (fails 3/3 at good end) | n/a | n/a | correct |

Score: 4 of 6 correct (key kept privately, not in either repo). Both single-regression behavioural signatures and the refusal were
right; the three token-budget signatures are the weak spot.

## Honest notes
- Budget signatures remain unreliable: every token regression (R1 tool schema, R2 search_help rule) inflates every category, so a
  per-category budget signature blames whichever commit crosses 1.5x last. order_status was assigned 59c8b10 although the
  order_status-specific regression is earlier; reverting 59c8b10 left tokens above the limit (revert test failed, flagged
  "multiple regressions likely"). refund_outside_policy landed on an unrelated later commit (5cee99b) with an inconclusive revert.
  refund_within_policy matches the key only because 59c8b10 is a contributor; its revert test also failed (0/3 -> 0/3).
- Smart was slower than plain on the two budget signatures that needed many rounds (+12, +6 rounds); it won on the two behavioural ones
  (-6, -1) and tied on one. Planner context 20-24k tokens with the graph vs 43-47k reading the raw range.
- A reply_contains signature (os3, 1 of 3 runs) was seen once and dropped as unreproduced (`signatures_unconfirmed`).
- ca/ms cases do not exist at the good end, so the baseline excludes them (and es2); no ca/ms/po/es budget signatures surfaced.
- Neatlogs span divergence still unavailable (TRACE_FINALIZATION_FAILED), so the planner ranked on graph impact and checkpoint intent.
- LLM proxy cache (`.agentbisect/llm_cache`, shared with earlier runs) replayed some identical prompts: calibrate 136 calls (112 real CLI,
  24 cache hits); investigate 659 calls (564 real, 96 hits, 1 error, 2 invalid-output retries); compare 5 signatures mostly cache
  replays (1079 calls with 88 real CLI by the third compare; final counter lost because the proxy stats file was written empty).
  Rate-limit events: 0, retries: 0 in calibrate and investigate; no 429 backoff was provoked.
- Not run: `compare` for es2 (refused, nothing to bisect).
import type {
  AnchorHTMLAttributes,
  ButtonHTMLAttributes,
  ComponentType,
  ReactNode,
  Ref,
} from "react";
import { cx, sortCx } from "@/utils/cx";
import { directionalIconClass } from "@/utils/directional-icon";

/**
 * Figma source: Board UI → Buttons (node 3656:13819).
 *
 * Variant matrix from Figma:
 *   Type     = Primary | Secondary | Ghost | Danger
 *   Size     = Medium  | Small | Xs
 *   State    = Default | Hover | Active | Disabled        (CSS pseudo)
 *   OnlyIcon = false   | true
 *
 * Sizing (1:1 with Figma):
 *
 *                       Medium                    Small                     Xs
 *   container          h=36, p=8,   r=10         h=32, px=8 py=6, r=8      h=24, px=8, r=4
 *   gap                 2px                       2px                      1.33px→1
 *   icon                20×20                     18×18                    14×14
 *   label wrapper       px=4                      px=2                     px=2
 *   text style          Body 1/Medium             Body 1/Medium            Caption 1/Semibold
 *   icon-only square    36×36 (content-derived)   32×32 (forced size)      24×24 (forced size)
 *
 * `xs` is the smallest tier — first needed for the calendar template's
 * event-details modal ("Join" / edit-icon buttons, node 3920:10954), which
 * scales every dimension down by the same ~0.667 factor from Figma; the
 * table above rounds those to clean pixel values rather than reproducing
 * the fractional source numbers.
 *
 * Icons are rendered by the component itself via the `leadingIcon` /
 * `trailingIcon` props so the consumer can't pass the wrong size. Pass
 * a Remix Icon component reference (`RiAddLine`, not `<RiAddLine />`).
 *
 * For icon-only buttons:
 *   <Button iconOnly leadingIcon={RiAddLine} aria-label="Add" />
 *
 * The HTML `type` prop is preserved; Figma's "Type" enum is renamed to
 * `variant` to avoid the clash.
 */

type ButtonVariant = "primary" | "secondary" | "ghost" | "danger";
type ButtonSize = "medium" | "small" | "xs";

type IconComponent = ComponentType<{
  className?: string;
  "aria-hidden"?: boolean | "true" | "false";
}>;

export interface ButtonProps
  extends Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "children"> {
  variant?: ButtonVariant;
  size?: ButtonSize;
  iconOnly?: boolean;
  leadingIcon?: IconComponent;
  trailingIcon?: IconComponent;
  children?: ReactNode;
  ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement>;
}

export interface ButtonLinkProps
  extends Omit<AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement>, "children"> {
  variant?: ButtonVariant;
  size?: ButtonSize;
  iconOnly?: boolean;
  leadingIcon?: IconComponent;
  trailingIcon?: IconComponent;
  children?: ReactNode;
  ref?: Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>;
}

const styles = sortCx({
  base: [
    "inline-flex items-center justify-center gap-0.5 whitespace-nowrap overflow-hidden",
    "font-sans select-none cursor-pointer",
# 2. Investigate from a bad trace (or --detection ID, or --issue URL)
uv run agentbisect investigate --trace <trace-id> --repo ../support-agent-demo \
    --strategy smart --all-signatures --all-categories --llm-proxy auto

# or skip neatlogs and name the range yourself
uv run agentbisect investigate --trace <trace-id> --repo ../support-agent-demo \
    --fixtures path/to/bundle.json --good 1b40b27 --bad 0ecffc0

uv run agentbisect status [ID]          # investigations and their steps
uv run agentbisect resume ID            # continue after an interruption
uv run agentbisect compare ID           # plain vs smart: eval rounds and cost
uv run agentbisect summary --format md  # per-signature results table
uv run agentbisect report ID            # Markdown + HTML report in evidence/
```

```bash
# Fix + verify on a saved investigation (default fd47af3916, the R3 refund-amount culprit).
# Works on a throwaway clone of the demo repo; needs a logged-in `claude` CLI.
scripts/demo_fix_verify.sh [investigation-id]

# or step by step
uv run agentbisect fix ID --llm-proxy auto --out DIR
uv run agentbisect verify-fix ID --commit SHA --llm-proxy auto   # exit 0 verified, 1 not, 2 inconclusive
```

State lives in `.agentbisect/` (atomic writes, resumable mid-step). Run `uv run agentbisect --help` for all flags.

### Span divergence and the fixture fallback

Live span divergence reads multi-span traces from neatlogs. At the time of writing, those traces finalize as `dlq` with zero spans (see [Next steps](#next-steps)), so for the demo the same step runs on a **recorded fixture**:

origin	https://github.com/jaxsonsprinkles/agentbisect.git (push)
